bullets.title: AMD MI500 Leads Nvidia Rubin Ultra in Key AI Chip Specs; HBM4 Samsung Deal Imminent
bullets.body: Multiple accounts flag AMD's MI500 as ahead of Nvidia's Rubin Ultra in optical interconnects, HBM capability, 4-die packaging, and scale-up domain. Separately, AMD is reported close to signing a definitive large-scale HBM4 supply agreement with Samsung. Jefferies raised its AMD price target to $640 from $515, maintaining Buy, citing AI accelerator TAM now seen at $1.4T by 2030 (up from $1T) with agentic AI comprising ~50% of that.

bullets.title: Intel 2Q26 Blowout: Revenue $16.1B vs $14.3B Est; 3Q Guide Also Beats
bullets.body: Intel's 2Q26 revenue of $16.1B was described as the strongest growth in 15+ years, well above the $14.3B consensus. 3Q26 guidance of $16.3B also beats consensus of $15.1B with 42% gross margin guided. One analyst sets a $136 price target based on 5x 2027E book value and 34x 2028E EPS, citing strong data center momentum.

bullets.title: Mag 7 Premarket: Tesla +1.3% Bounce After 15% Plunge; Nvidia Only Decliner
bullets.body: Tesla led Mag 7 names in premarket recovery (+1.3%) following a ~15% drop on Thursday. Microsoft +1.1%, Alphabet +0.7%, Meta +0.7%, Amazon +0.5%, Apple +0.2%. Nvidia was the sole decliner at -0.4%. Separately, TSLA is noted as down ~22% since Michael Burry opened his short position.

bullets.title: Google's Anthropic Stake Now Worth ~$124B; SpaceX Stake ~$94B
bullets.body: Google's equity stake in Anthropic is valued at approximately $124 billion, with its SpaceX stake at ~$94 billion, underscoring the growing hidden value in Alphabet's venture portfolio.

bullets.title: Token Costs at 3.5-Month Lows, Erasing Agentic Bounce; Hyperscaler Index Also Weak
bullets.body: Token costs have fully retraced the agentic AI rally and are at 3.5-month lows. The hyperscaler index is also at lows. Goldman Delta-1 warns that AI bond repricing is 'punitive for equity multiples' even as hyperscalers maintain low balance sheet leverage, flagging reflexivity as the key risk dynamic.

bullets.title: Hyperscalers Raising Large Debt/Equity as Returns Deteriorate
bullets.body: One fintwit commentator notes an emerging dynamic: hyperscalers now need to raise large amounts of debt and/or equity, while trailing returns on both are weakening — a capital cycle concern for the AI infrastructure build-out.

bullets.title: Samsung & SK Hynix to Announce 'Very Large-Scale' U.S. Tech Contracts
bullets.body: South Korea's presidential policy chief announced Samsung and SK Hynix will sign major long-term chip supply agreements with U.S. technology companies, timed to President Lee Jae-myung's Silicon Valley visit.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Equipment Delivery Times Doubling, Pressuring Chipmakers
bullets.body: A report flagged on fintwit notes semiconductor equipment delivery times have doubled, putting chipmakers under increasing supply-side pressure — a potential constraint on capacity expansion timelines.

bullets.title: American Express Q2 Beats on EPS; Raises Revenue Growth Guide to +10%
bullets.body: AXP reported Q2 EPS of $4.53 vs. $4.41 estimate (beat) on revenue of $19.64B vs. $19.69B estimate (slight miss). Billed Business of $455.8B beat estimates. FY26 EPS guidance maintained at $17.30–$17.90 while revenue growth guidance was nudged up to +10% from +9%–+10%.

bullets.title: Verizon Q2 EBITDA Beat; Raises FY EPS Guide for Second Consecutive Quarter
bullets.body: VZ reported adj. EBITDA of $13.7B vs. $13.65B estimate, with operating revenue of $34.3B missing the $35.17B estimate. FY adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $4.99–$5.04 from $4.95–$4.99, marking the second consecutive quarter of upward guidance revision.

bullets.title: Oil Drops Sharply: Brent Below $97, WTI Below $89 Despite Geopolitical Risk Premium
bullets.body: Brent crude fell over $4 to ~$96.48/bbl and WTI dropped over $3 to ~$88.82/bbl, with one analyst estimating Iran/Houthi geopolitical factors add $49 to the price while demand weakness offsets $10. Political betting markets expect supply disruption to persist while oil futures price a swift resolution — a notable divergence.

bullets.title: Initial Jobless Claims Hit 187k — Lowest Since 1969
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims dropped to 187k from 209k prior, the lowest reading since 1969. Continuing claims also remain below year-ago levels on a YoY basis, signaling continued labor market resilience.

bullets.title: Global Treasury Yields Hit 16-Year High at 3.68%
bullets.body: The Bloomberg Global Treasury Index yield rose to 3.68%, surpassing the 2008 global financial crisis peak — a macro headwind for equity valuations and duration-sensitive assets.

bullets.title: ECB Officials Signal Inflation Upside Risk; $100 Oil a Key Concern
bullets.body: Multiple ECB officials (Simkus, Rehn) flagged that inflation risks remain to the upside, with Simkus specifically warning that $100 oil 'will have repercussions on inflation.' Rehn noted the energy crisis is 'still ongoing' and no second-round effects are visible yet, with the ECB deferring further decisions to September.

bullets.title: Trump Forced-Labor Tariffs on 60 Countries; EU and Brazil Push Back
bullets.body: The Trump administration imposed forced-labor duties on 60 countries. EU's Kallas questioned U.S. rationale, and Brazil characterized the tariffs as 'arbitrary and unjustified,' raising risks of further trade retaliation.

bullets.title: Diesel Prices Up 10% Since July 5, Adding Input Cost Pressure
bullets.body: U.S. diesel prices have risen 10% since July 5, described as a key input cost driver for consumer goods, groceries, and construction — a potential contributor to near-term CPI upside.

bullets.title: AXTI: Possible Workarounds for China Permit Restrictions Under Review
bullets.body: One fintwit account highlights that AXTI may have potential workarounds for its China permit restrictions, though the author notes limited clarity on full viability, describing feasibility as 'possible to a certain extent' pending further industry checks.

bullets.title: SPCX Bonds Hit All-Time Low at 87, Down 7.7% YTD, Trading Near High-Yield Averages
bullets.body: SpaceX bonds (SPCX) hit an all-time low of 87, down 7.7% YTD, and are now trading as a B-rated credit approaching Caa high-yield averages — notable credit deterioration in a closely watched private-company proxy.
